close: On a bad day, people steady themselves on your calm.
Your best ideas sit idle between one emergency and the next.
Everyone you live with moves at your speed, even on a lazy Sunday.
In a stalled room, your first move gets everyone else going.
The weight of everything you run lands on your shoulders alone.
Those close to you get looked after and seldom get a say.
Much of what gets done around you gets done because you stayed.
Your body keeps the bill for every hard mile.
With you, whole teams reach finish lines they would have walked away from.
You are usually the only one in the room who will.
What you want is to be heard and still be asked back.
Your voice fills the space their own words were meant for.
The moments people talk about afterwards tend to be yours.
Many of your best ideas end up half built and never shown whole.
The group meets your change while the old version is still running.
Your work is never mistaken for anyone else's.
You pay for the spotlight in friendships that cool while you shine.
Around you, quieter people find the nerve to try things they would not try alone.
The mood of a room reaches you before anyone has named it.
Underneath, you want to be understood without explaining yourself.
Your quick replies leave their stories half told.
Part of you would love a guide, and that wish goes unsaid.
Friends with skills to share seldom get the pleasure of showing you.
Your decisions come late and hold up for years.
Some good chances go to quicker people while you are still deciding.
What they get from you in the end is a word you will stand by.
Half the good ideas in your circle started as something you pointed at.
Good things within reach go by while you look further out.
Your partners get half of your mind on the shared work.
Whole projects exist because you went first while others were still talking.
Your life fills with things you began and never saw through.
The slow work of finishing falls to whoever came along with you.
More than one friend got through a hard year with your help.
Your savings stay thin through even the best years.
Nobody near you goes without for long.
Others find their nerve by watching you move.
You take the first hit alone, every time.
Your lead gives slower friends a path already cut.
What you want is a rival worth keeping up with.
Your body runs on empty for days after each finish line.
Your friends get very few slow afternoons in your company.
Your partners never face a bad loss by themselves.
Half of every good year of yours belongs to someone else.
Their savings rise and fall with your choices.
Others build careers on ideas that started with you.
Those around you miss the thrill of the search.
Several friends got through their worst year under your roof.
Your home is seldom fully yours, and your evenings belong to guests.
Your guests get time to mend without a clock running.
Years of your life go to someone else's schedule.
Your patience leaves them to find the hard part on their own.
Anyone who has your yes builds on it without a second thought.
Some of your years go to promises made by a younger you.
Around you, people say yes more carefully and mean it.
Nobody questions a place you hold, because everyone saw you work for it.
Promotions you deserved have gone to louder people.
Your team spends extra years proving what you already see in them.
Everyone around you is sure of the ground under their feet.
Your fairness takes some of the warmth out of home.
A friend in real trouble gets the same answer from you as anyone.
Your work is still standing when quicker efforts have fallen.
A part of you still aches for the dream you set aside.
Your family sees the result and very little of the making.
Your household weathers bad years that sink other families.
Whole seasons of your life pass without a single treat.
Your family never wonders where the next month's money comes from.
The person beside you has never once doubted you.
Some of your choices were made once and never made again.
Your partner gets all of your time and few of your words.
What you build is yours from the first nail to the last.
Your hardest weeks are carried on one pair of shoulders.
People who would gladly help seldom get the chance to be needed by you.
Nobody rushes you into a decision you would regret.
Some doors shut while you are still walking towards them.
Days out with you often split into two groups.
Friends never have to guess which you will turn up.
Some tenderness passes you by.
In a hard week, the people close to you get no softer version of you.
Your kitchen, your toolbox and your time are open to whoever walks in.
Underneath is a wish to be loved for who you are, empty-handed.
The people you love rarely get to say what they wanted from you.
Your home fills with useful, lovely pieces nobody else would have made.
Fine work of yours sits in drawers, unseen and unthanked.
Friends who drop by to talk often find your eyes on your work.
People breathe easier at your table, and nobody feels hurried there.
Some of your bigger chances drift past unclaimed.
Those you teach learn without fear of getting it wrong in front of you.
